woman-song.name: The woman
woman-song.role: Woman who speaks about her desire and her work
woman-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
woman-song.importance: She asks for meetings and describes harm during her search. Her words give her wishes a direct voice.
woman-song.connections: She seeks her lover and speaks to the women of Jerusalem.

lover-song.name: The lover
lover-song.role: Man who invites and praises the woman
lover-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
lover-song.importance: His praise uses the surrounding world to express his desire.
lover-song.connections: She calls him her beloved and her friend.

women-song.name: The women of Jerusalem
women-song.role: Women who hear and answer the lovers
women-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
women-song.importance: Their questions lead the woman to explain why she wants him.
women-song.connections: They ask about the lover and offer to help find him.

brothers-song.name: The brothers
brothers-song.role: Family members who discuss work and their sister’s future
brothers-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
brothers-song.importance: Their decisions show family control. The woman later gives her own answer.
brothers-song.connections: The woman describes angry brothers. Later brothers discuss a young sister.

watchmen-song.name: The watchmen
watchmen-song.role: Men who patrol the city and its walls
watchmen-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
watchmen-song.importance: The later search includes their violence against her. Their public role does not make her safe.
watchmen-song.connections: The woman meets watchmen during two night searches.

solomon-guards-song.name: Solomon’s guards
solomon-guards-song.role: Sixty armed men around Solomon’s carriage
solomon-guards-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon-guards-song.importance: The royal procession has protection unavailable to the woman during her later search.
solomon-guards-song.connections: They carry swords because of danger at night.

solomon-mother-song.name: Solomon’s mother
solomon-mother-song.role: Mother who crowns Solomon in the wedding scene
solomon-mother-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon-mother-song.importance: Her crown joins family honor with the king’s public celebration.
solomon-mother-song.connections: The poem names her relationship but does not give her name.

woman-mother-song.name: The woman’s mother
woman-mother-song.role: Mother whose house appears in the woman’s words
woman-mother-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
woman-mother-song.importance: The home connects her desire with the family that raised her.
woman-mother-song.connections: The woman brings her lover toward her mother’s house.

pharaoh-song.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh-song.role: Unnamed Egyptian ruler mentioned in a comparison
pharaoh-song.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pharaoh-song.importance: The image gives his praise the force of a royal horse. Pharaoh does not act in this poem.
pharaoh-song.connections: The lover compares the woman with a horse among Pharaoh’s chariots.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.role: King named in the title and royal scenes
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: His wealth provides comparisons with the lovers’ desire. The book does not clearly identify him as the lover.
solomon.connections: His carriage, mother, and vineyard appear in the poems.

david.name: David
david.role: King named in the lover’s tower comparison
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: Shields and a tower give the praise an image of strength.
david.connections: The lover compares the woman’s neck with David’s tower.
